interest: Shows pre-Pearl Harbor Japan retaliating against British visa applicants in Manchuria, highlighting unequal treatment of British versus American nationals.
overview: Consul Gourley reports from Harbin that Japan's Foreign Office centralized and stalled British visa approvals in retaliation for British visa curbs, illustrated by a British banker blocked at Dairen while his American wife's visa cleared easily.

subfiles.about: Cover despatch transmitting to the Department of State a copy of despatch No. 73 to the American Embassy in Peiping concerning Japanese visa obstruction against British subjects.
subfiles.from: Louis H. Gourley, American Consul at Harbin
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 107: Gourley forwards his confidential despatch to Gauss detailing Japan's obstructive visa policy toward British subjects.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 107 from Gourley (Harbin) to Secretary of State enclosing despatch on Japanese visa policy

subfiles.about: Confidential report detailing the Japanese Foreign Office's retaliatory policy of obstructing visas for British subjects, illustrated by the case of a British banker transiting Dairen.
subfiles.from: Louis H. Gourley, American Consul at Harbin
subfiles.summary: Gourley reports Japan required British visa requests routed through Tokyo in retaliation for British restrictions on Japanese nationals; a British banker was delayed at Dairen though his American-passport wife got her visa easily two weeks earlier.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 73 from Gourley (Harbin) to Gauss (Peiping) on Japanese obstructive visa policy
subfiles.to: Clarence E. Gauss, American Ambassador at Peiping
